newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude says FDA clears Tendril DX lead.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude says FDA clears Tendril DX lead.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc said it received U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for market release of the Pacesetter Tendril DX steroid-eluting active fixation pacing lead.
A pacing lead is an insulated wire that connects the heart muscle to an electronic heart-rhythm management device, such as a pacemaker, implanted in the body.
The Tendril DX has an extendable-retractable helix tip designed for secure placement in the interior wall of the upper or lower chamber of the heart, St. Jude said.
The tip electrode contains a steroid that is released when the helix enters the heart. The steroid reduces tissue inflammation common with non-steroid-eluting fixation leads.
The Tendril DX lead tip is coated with titanium nitride, which improves its the lead's sensing ability, and is insulated with silicone, said St. Jude.
Pacesetter is part of St. Jude's new Cardiac Rhythm Management Division, which also markets Ventritex-branded defibrillators and pacemakers, St. Jude said.
